title: Fibrant-replacement path model recognizes homotopy-cartesian squares
statement: Use small simplicial sets, internal functor simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], with the functorial Kan--Quillen model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. For a commutative square with maps $a:Q\to X$, $b:Q\to Y$, $f:X\to Z$, $g:Y\to Z$ and $fa=gb$, call it homotopy cartesian when there exist factorizations $X\xrightarrow{i}X_f\xrightarrow{f_f}Z$ and $Y\xrightarrow{j}Y_f\xrightarrow{g_f}Z$ with $i,j$ weak equivalences and $f_f,g_f$ Kan fibrations such that the induced map $Q\to X_f\times_ZY_f$ is a weak equivalence. Let $r:\mathrm{id}\to R$ be any functorial fibrant replacement obtained by factoring each map to $\Delta^0$ into a trivial cofibration followed by a Kan fibration. Put $$P_R=RX\times_{RZ,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,RZ)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,RZ}RY.$$ Then the original square is homotopy cartesian if and only if the map $RQ\to P_R$ with coordinates $Ra,Rb$ and the constant path at $(Rf)(Ra)=(Rg)(Rb)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. No Kan or nonemptiness assumption on $Q,X,Y,Z$ is imposed.
